item.title: Downtown Pensacola Lights Up Holiday Season Nov. 4 with Santa, Shopping, and Half-Million Lights
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Downtown Pensacola is kicking off the holiday season Wednesday, November 4th with a full slate of festive events centered on Palafox Street. Santa will arrive at 3:30 p.m. in front of the Pensacola Museum of History for photos and selfies until 4:45 p.m., when he'll flip the switch to illuminate more than half a million holiday lights stretching…
item.content:encoded:
Downtown Pensacola is kicking off the holiday season Wednesday, November 4th with a full slate of festive events centered on Palafox Street. Santa will arrive at 3:30 p.m. in front of the Pensacola Museum of History for photos and selfies until 4:45 p.m., when he'll flip the switch to illuminate more than half a million holiday lights stretching along Palafox and surrounding areas.

The evening's anchor event is the 10th Annual Holiday Haul, running from 5 p.m. to 8 p.m., featuring an open house atmosphere across downtown shops, galleries, and restaurants with live music, pop-ups, giveaways, and free trolley rides. The special Holiday Lights Edition of the Palafox Market will operate from 3:30 p.m. to 8 p.m. in Plaza Ferdinand, with local vendors selling homemade gifts, baked goods, and art. Visitors can also expect to see the Grinch and a mini-train circulating around Plaza Ferdinand throughout the evening.

The Downtown Improvement Board and local merchants are also launching the "All I Want" Holiday Giveaway, running through December 20th. Shoppers earn one raffle entry for every $10 spent at downtown businesses, with weekly prizes and a $1,000 grand prize in downtown gift cards. Double-entry opportunities occur on November 4th and Shop Small Saturday, November 28th. More details are available at www.downtownpensacola.com/AllIWant.

item.title: ECSO adds security to Ernest Ward Middle after TikTok threat investigation
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Escambia County Sheriff's Office is investigating a threat posted on TikTok targeting Ernest Ward Middle School in Walnut Hill, with extra deputies positioned on campus Tuesday as a precaution. According to the ECSO, investigators became aware of the social media post Monday and immediately launched an active inquiry into the matter. While…
item.content:encoded:
The Escambia County Sheriff's Office is investigating a threat posted on TikTok targeting Ernest Ward Middle School in Walnut Hill, with extra deputies positioned on campus Tuesday as a precaution.

According to the ECSO, investigators became aware of the social media post Monday and immediately launched an active inquiry into the matter. While details about the nature of the specific threat were not immediately disclosed, the agency determined the situation warranted heightened security presence at the school.

The deployment of additional law enforcement at the campus reflects standard protocol when schools face credible threats. Parents and guardians in the Ernest Ward attendance zone were likely notified of the increased security measures. The ECSO investigation is ongoing.

item.content:encoded:
The University of West Florida's Center for Cybersecurity and AI has been selected to participate in a national initiative aimed at measuring how cybersecurity education affects the workforce, economy, and broader mission outcomes, according to WKRG News 5.

The selection underscores UWF's growing prominence in the cybersecurity field and positions the university to contribute research data that will help track the real-world impact of cybersecurity training programs across the country.

Details about the specific goals, timeline, and funding for the national center initiative were not immediately available. The development adds another credential to UWF's expanding role in preparing the regional workforce for careers in one of the nation's fastest-growing tech sectors.

item.title: Donalds, Jolly Make Final Campaign Push in Escambia County

The…
item.content:encoded:
With Election Day just over a week away, Florida's gubernatorial candidates brought their competing visions to Escambia County on Tuesday. Republican Byron Donalds held a rally at Jerry's Drive-In, while Democratic candidate David Jolly campaigned at Seville Quarter, each making a final pitch to voters in the pivotal Northwest Florida region.

The dual appearances underscore the importance of Escambia County in statewide races. The county has long been a political battleground, and both campaigns are investing resources in mobilizing supporters before voters head to the polls next week.

item.content:encoded:
Families interested in exploring educational options within Escambia County Public Schools can attend the annual School Choice Expo this Thursday, October 29, from 6 to 7:30 p.m. at Washington High School.

Representatives from ECPS Career Academies and Choice Schools will be on hand to discuss their programs and answer questions about enrollment, curriculum, and student support services. The event typically draws more than 1,000 attendees seeking information about specialized programs and school choices available across the district.

The expo is free and open to families at all grade levels. Those planning to attend should arrive early, as the event usually draws a large crowd.

Seth Malaki Slavey was charged with violating Florida's street racing and stunt driving law, as well as operating a vehicle at a speed exceeding the limit by 50 mph or…
item.content:encoded:
A 19-year-old Cantonment resident faces felony charges after Florida Highway Patrol caught him racing at 93 mph through a work zone on Highway 29, according to an arrest report.

Seth Malaki Slavey was charged with violating Florida's street racing and stunt driving law, as well as operating a vehicle at a speed exceeding the limit by 50 mph or more — a serious traffic violation that carries significant penalties.

The FHP clocked Slavey's excessive speed in an active work zone, where construction crews and equipment are typically present, creating heightened danger to workers and other motorists. Work zone speeding violations carry enhanced penalties under Florida law designed to protect road workers.

item.content:encoded: The Town of Century has secured nearly half a million dollars in state funding to renovate an industrial building aimed at spurring local economic development. According to reporting from North Escambia, Governor Ron DeSantis awarded the $499,500 grant through the Florida Job Growth Grant Fund. The money will go toward renovating an existing town-owned building at 9082 Industrial Boulevard within the Century Industrial Park. The project is expected to help attract businesses and create jobs in the Santa Rosa County community.

item.title: Gulf Islands National Seashore reopens all areas after Hurricane Isaias
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Nearly three weeks after Hurricane Isaias made landfall in the Florida Panhandle, Gulf Islands National Seashore is moving forward with a full reopening of the park, according to WKRG News 5. The seashore, which spans portions of Santa Rosa County and the surrounding region, had implemented phased closures following the storm's impact. The…
item.content:encoded:
Nearly three weeks after Hurricane Isaias made landfall in the Florida Panhandle, Gulf Islands National Seashore is moving forward with a full reopening of the park, according to WKRG News 5.

The seashore, which spans portions of Santa Rosa County and the surrounding region, had implemented phased closures following the storm's impact. The reopening clears all remaining restricted areas, allowing visitors to return to beaches, trails, and other facilities throughout the national park system.

Hurricane Isaias struck the Florida Panhandle earlier this month, forcing initial closures and assessments across multiple public recreation areas. Park officials have been evaluating storm damage and clearing debris to ensure visitor safety before restoring full access.

item.content:encoded:
Jubilee Church is opening its doors Friday night for Glow Fest 2026, a free community event designed to give local families a safe Halloween alternative filled with games, candy, face painting, and prizes.

The event runs from 5:30 PM to 8:00 PM at the church, located at 5910 N W Street. There's no admission charge, and organizers say there will be activities for children of all ages, along with glowing lights and attractions throughout the evening.

While families are welcome to bring a bag of candy to contribute to the festivities, it's not required to attend. According to the church, Glow Fest is part of its commitment to building relationships and giving back to the Pensacola community. More information is available at www.jubileepensacola.com.

The facility, located at 2000 E. Lloyd Street, has been operating as a central hub for hurricane recovery assistance. Residents can visit through Friday to request help accessing…
item.content:encoded:
The City of Pensacola is reminding residents that the Bayview Senior Center Multi-Agency Resource Center will close its doors for the final time on Friday, October 30.

The facility, located at 2000 E. Lloyd Street, has been operating as a central hub for hurricane recovery assistance. Residents can visit through Friday to request help accessing food, water, housing, recovery services, and other storm-related support.

According to the city's announcement, anyone still needing recovery resources or information should visit before the Friday deadline.

item.title: Okaloosa County to unveil Charters of Freedom monument in Crestview
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Okaloosa County commissioners will dedicate a Charters of Freedom monument Tuesday, November 3rd, outside the Crestview Courthouse. The ceremony is scheduled for mid-morning, around 10:30 to 11 a.m., immediately following the regular board meeting. The monument features stainless-steel replicas of the Declaration of Independence, U.S.…
item.content:encoded:
Okaloosa County commissioners will dedicate a Charters of Freedom monument Tuesday, November 3rd, outside the Crestview Courthouse. The ceremony is scheduled for mid-morning, around 10:30 to 11 a.m., immediately following the regular board meeting.

The monument features stainless-steel replicas of the Declaration of Independence, U.S. Constitution, Bill of Rights, and Civil Rights Amendments. The display was donated by Foundation Forward Inc., a North Carolina nonprofit that has distributed similar monuments to communities across 17 states.

This is one of two Charters of Freedom monuments coming to Okaloosa County. A second monument will be unveiled November 11th at Women Veterans Park during a Veterans Day event. "This monument brings our attention to the lasting impacts these documents have had on our country," said Okaloosa County Board Chairman Trey Goodwin in a statement.

The decision removes a significant financial incentive from the development equation, but developers have signaled commitment to…
item.content:encoded:
Developers of the $310 million Reverb by Hard Rock Hotel project in downtown Pensacola have withdrawn their request for a $58 million tax rebate, according to Florida Trend, but say the project will proceed regardless.

The decision removes a significant financial incentive from the development equation, but developers have signaled commitment to moving forward with the mixed-use hotel and entertainment complex despite the loss of the tax rebate support.

The Reverb project has been a major part of Pensacola's downtown redevelopment strategy, and the confirmation that it will continue without the public incentive should provide clarity to the community about the project's trajectory and timeline.

item.content:encoded:
Pensacola's waterfront hosted its first Blues on the Bluff festival Sunday, drawing music fans to Calvert's in the Heights along Scenic Highway for an afternoon of live blues performances. The inaugural event took advantage of views overlooking Pensacola Bay and the natural amphitheater setting the bluff provides, creating what organizers and attendees described as an ideal showcase for the genre's soulful sound.

The festival represents a new addition to Pensacola's growing music event calendar, tapping into the region's cultural heritage and appeal to both locals and visitors. With the waterfront location and scenic backdrop, Blues on the Bluff appears positioned to become a recurring fixture in the community's entertainment offerings.

item.title: Florida Gaming Control Commission Wins International Regulatory Excellence Award
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Florida Gaming Control Commission has been recognized with the Regulatory Excellence Award from the International Association of Gaming Regulators, honoring the young agency's coordinated efforts to combat illegal gambling across the state. Since its creation in July 2022, the FGCC has seized more than 14,000 illegal slot machines and…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Gaming Control Commission has been recognized with the Regulatory Excellence Award from the International Association of Gaming Regulators, honoring the young agency's coordinated efforts to combat illegal gambling across the state.

Since its creation in July 2022, the FGCC has seized more than 14,000 illegal slot machines and recovered over $24 million in illegal gambling proceeds. In the past year alone, the agency shut down 184 illegal gambling arcades and made 160 arrests. The commission's investigations have also helped law enforcement target illegal narcotics, illegal firearms, and dog betting rings tied to criminal gambling operations.

"This demonstrates that FGCC is a great team doing things correctly," said FGCC Chair Julie Brown in a statement. The award recognizes the agency's impact as Florida's first statewide law enforcement agency created since 1967. IAGR CEO Kevin Mullally praised the commission's collaborative approach, saying its strategy "illustrates the power of collaboration" in combating illegal gambling.

Attorney General James Uthmeier said his office will continue working with the FGCC to push for tougher criminal penalties against illegal gambling operators. Legal gambling in Florida is restricted to eight licensed pari-mutuel facilities in Miami-Dade and Broward counties, as well as certain facilities operated by the Seminole Tribe of Florida. Residents can report suspected illegal gambling at FLGaming.gov/File-a-Report or by calling 850-880-3433.

item.title: IMPACT 100 Awards Record $1.313 Million to 13 Northwest Florida Nonprofits
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Thirteen nonprofits serving Escambia and Santa Rosa counties will each receive $101,000 after IMPACT 100 Pensacola Bay Area announced its annual grant recipients Sunday. A record 1,313 members allowed the organization to award $1.313 million this year. Recipients cover five areas: arts, education, environment and…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Thirteen nonprofits serving Escambia and Santa Rosa counties will each receive $101,000 after IMPACT 100 Pensacola Bay Area announced its annual grant recipients Sunday.

A record 1,313 members allowed the organization to award $1.313 million this year.

Recipients cover five areas: arts, education, environment and recreation, family services, and health and wellness.

Ballet Pensacola will use its grant to update costumes and lighting for "The Nutcracker," while the Pensacola Children's Chorus plans to invest in transportation and community performances.

The Naval Aviation Museum Foundation will receive $101,000 for its Flight Adventure Deck project.

The Santa Rosa Education Foundation was selected for an expansion of its Little Red School House program, while the Pensacola MESS Hall will use its grant for expanded after-school science programming.

Keep Pensacola Beautiful received funding for reforestation and invasive-species removal.

The Pensacola and Perdido Bays Estuary Program was selected for an environmental education and stewardship project.

Pensacola Habitat for Humanity will receive $101,000 for a partnership with Family Promise aimed at helping families with housing.

South Santa Rosa Interfaith Ministries and Life Options Clinic were also selected in the family category.

Health and Hope Clinic received funding to expand dental care, while 4EVR DEZ and The Seven Project received health-and-wellness grants.

This marks IMPACT 100 Pensacola Bay Area's 23rd year of grantmaking.

The organization says it has now awarded 190 grants totaling more than $20 million to nonprofits serving Escambia and Santa Rosa counties.

item.title: Santa Rosa County cancels Veterans Day Parade, plans ceremony at memorial
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Santa Rosa County Veterans Memorial Foundation has decided to cancel this year's Veterans Day Parade as the community continues cleanup and recovery following Hurricane Isaias, but organizers say the commitment to honoring veterans remains unchanged. Instead of the parade, the foundation is inviting the public to a Veterans Day Ceremony and…
item.content:encoded:
The Santa Rosa County Veterans Memorial Foundation has decided to cancel this year's Veterans Day Parade as the community continues cleanup and recovery following Hurricane Isaias, but organizers say the commitment to honoring veterans remains unchanged.

Instead of the parade, the foundation is inviting the public to a Veterans Day Ceremony and wreath-laying at the Santa Rosa County Veterans Memorial on November 11 at 11 a.m., weather permitting. Foundation President Tom Powers said in a statement that "our community's safety and recovery must come first."

Following the ceremony, attendees are invited to gather at American Legion Post #78 in Milton for a Flag Retirement ceremony, bonfire, and cookout. Grover's Restaurant is donating food, which will be served by local Santa Rosa County 4-H Club members and volunteers. "Now, more than ever, this is a time for our community to come together, honor our veterans, lend a helping hand, and support one another as we continue to recover and rebuild," Powers said.

item.title: Taddeo Pledges Insurance Accountability Plan in Pensacola Roundtable
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Democratic candidate for Florida Chief Financial Officer Annette Taddeo held a roundtable discussion in Pensacola on Monday to address the state's ongoing insurance crisis, fielding concerns from residents about rising homeowners insurance costs and calling for stronger consumer protections. Taddeo, a former state senator, pledged to release a…
item.content:encoded:
Democratic candidate for Florida Chief Financial Officer Annette Taddeo held a roundtable discussion in Pensacola on Monday to address the state's ongoing insurance crisis, fielding concerns from residents about rising homeowners insurance costs and calling for stronger consumer protections.

Taddeo, a former state senator, pledged to release a report card evaluating insurance companies' financial stability within her first 100 days in office if elected. She also highlighted her previous legislative work pushing for greater transparency around insurers' affiliated companies, arguing that Florida needs an independent watchdog willing to hold the industry accountable regardless of political affiliation.

Joining the discussion was Dr. Frank Collige, a former Republican CFO primary candidate who has since backed Taddeo's campaign. Collige criticized the Department of Financial Services for failing to adequately police insurers when they violate the law, and pointed out that the CFO's office has conducted zero audits of insurance companies. "We need a CFO who will actually do audits, who will actually hold people accountable," Collige said.

Insurance expert Gary Rosen, Ph.D., also participated in the roundtable. Taddeo's campaign centers on three priorities: affordability, accountability, and anti-corruption. More information on her candidacy is available at annettetaddeo.com.
